What I learned putting a chatbot in my bakery

Posted by Yaw Mensah on 21 August 2024 · 6 min read

Last year my sister and I decided to try an AI chatbot for the bakery's WhatsApp orders. We are a small shop in Tema with five staff, and on weekends we were missing orders because nobody could answer the phone and serve customers at the same time. This post is an honest account of what worked and what did not.

The setup took much longer than the sales video promised. It was two weekends of work before the bot could answer basic questions about prices and opening hours. The hardest part was writing down our own menu in a structured way, because until then the prices only lived in my sister's head and on a chalkboard.

After three months, the bot handled about a third of incoming messages on its own. Customers liked getting an instant reply late at night, but many still preferred to talk to a person when ordering cakes for weddings or funerals. We kept a human in the loop for anything above 300 cedis.

The monthly cost was the real problem. The service charged in dollars, and when the exchange rate moved, our bill moved with it. In the end we switched to a cheaper plan with fewer features. If I were starting again, I would first spend a month just keeping clean digital records of orders, because that alone fixed half of our problems before any AI was involved.

My advice for other small business owners: start with one narrow task, measure it honestly, and do not believe anyone who says it will take an afternoon.
